title: Kunneth–Verdier isomorphism; the $\kappa$ map
statement:
Let $X,Y$ be separated finite-type schemes with dualizing complexes as
in [def-trf-dualizing-complex] (so the structure morphism $a_Y$ satisfies
the exceptional-adjoint admissibility of [def-trf-admissibility]), assume
that the product projection $p_X=\operatorname{id}_X\times a_Y:X\times Y\to X$
satisfies it as well, so that $p_X^!$ and the map
$\alpha_{\operatorname{id}_X,a_Y}$ of [def-sf-kv-maps] (ii) are defined, and
let $p_X,p_Y$ be the projections of $X\times Y$. For
$M\in D^b_{ctf}(X,A)$, $N\in D^b_{ctf}(Y,A)$, the canonical
comparison of [def-sf-kv-maps] (iv), formed with the geometric operations, is an isomorphism:

$$
\kappa_{M,N}:M\boxtimes_A^{\mathrm L}D_YN
\xrightarrow{\ \sim\ }
\RHom_A\bigl(p_Y^*N,\,p_X^!M\bigr),
$$

where $D_YN=\RHom_A(N,\omega_Y)$ is the dualizing functor of
[def-trf-dualizing-complex].

proof.text: Check the inputs for external Hom. The coefficient objects $A_X$ and $A_s$, concentrated in degree zero, are constructible in the sense of [def-weil-finite-torsion-constructibility] (take the one-piece partition): the constant coefficient sheaf is already locally constant with finite stalk $A$. They have Tor amplitude $[0,0]$ in the sense of [def-weil-finite-tor-amplitude], since tensoring the rank-one free coefficient sheaf with any sheaf in degree zero gives that sheaf in degree zero. The admissibility clause of [def-trf-admissibility] explicitly equips the restriction of the specified constructible exceptional inverse image with the functor type $Ra_Y^!:D^b_{ctf}(s,A)\to D^b_{ctf}(Y,A)$ and the adjunction $Ra_{Y!}\dashv Ra_Y^!$. Apply this restriction to $A_s$. By [def-trf-dualizing-complex], its value is $\omega_Y=Ra_Y^!A_s$, so $\omega_Y$ belongs to $D^b_{ctf}(Y,A)$. Thus all four inputs $(A_X,M,N,\omega_Y)$ meet the finite-Tor constructibility hypotheses of external Hom. These are the constructible exceptional functors throughout; no ambient right adjoint on all pro-etale sheaves is used. The identity morphism $\operatorname{id}_X$ is a separated finite-type $k$-morphism between finite-type $k$-schemes, so it is exceptionally admissible by [def-trf-admissibility], whose datum is available for every such morphism; its compact-support image is canonically the identity, so its specified exceptional adjoint $R\operatorname{id}_X^!$ is canonically isomorphic to the identity functor (uniqueness of right adjoints). This supplies the remaining exceptional-adjoint input.

source.place: Proof, first sentence: input hypotheses for the pairs $(A_X,M)$ and $(N,\omega_Y)$

proof.text: Use [def-sf-kv-maps] at its finite coefficient stage $\Lambda=A=A_{E,n}$, where it explicitly identifies its geometric functors and adjunction maps with the finite-stage exceptional-admissibility datum. Its $\mathbb D_YN=\RHom_A(N,Ra_Y^!A_s)$ is the same $D_YN$ as in [def-trf-dualizing-complex]. Here $p_Y^*$ in the item denotes the derived pullback $Lp_Y^*$ displayed in the current map definition. Apply [prop-trf-external-hom] on the separated finite-type schemes $X$ and $Y$ with $(E_1,L_1)=(A_X,M)$ and $(E_2,L_2)=(N,\omega_Y)$. This gives the specified evaluation-defined isomorphism $\beta:\RHom_A(A_X,M)\boxtimes_A^{\mathrm L}\RHom_A(N,\omega_Y)\xrightarrow{\sim}\RHom_A(A_X\boxtimes_A^{\mathrm L}N,M\boxtimes_A^{\mathrm L}\omega_Y)$. Use $D_YN=\RHom_A(N,\omega_Y)$ from [def-trf-dualizing-complex] and the unit identifications $\RHom_A(A_X,M)\cong M$, $A_X\boxtimes_A^{\mathrm L}N\cong Lp_Y^*N$ in [def-sf-kv-maps] (iv). We obtain an isomorphism $b:M\boxtimes_A^{\mathrm L}D_YN\xrightarrow{\sim}\RHom_A(Lp_Y^*N,M\boxtimes_A^{\mathrm L}\omega_Y)$, precisely the first arrow defining $\kappa_{M,N}$.

source.place: Proof, first sentence: apply external Hom to the two indicated pairs

proof.text: Apply [prop-trf-exceptional-kunneth] with $f_1=\operatorname{id}_X$, $f_2=a_Y:Y\to s$, $L_1=M$ and $L_2=A_s$. The coefficients are in $D^b_{ctf}$ by the hypotheses and step 1; the required exceptional adjoints are those of the identity, $a_Y$, and their product $p_X$, as assumed. Under the canonical target-base identification $X\times_k s\cong X$ and the unit identification for the constant coefficient $A_s$, the target coefficient is $L_1\boxtimes_A^{\mathrm L}L_2\cong M$; on the source side $R\operatorname{id}_X^!M\cong M$ by step 1, while $a_Y^!A_s=\omega_Y$ by [def-trf-dualizing-complex]. Thus its canonical comparison is the isomorphism $a=\alpha_{\operatorname{id}_X,a_Y}:M\boxtimes_A^{\mathrm L}\omega_Y\xrightarrow{\sim}p_X^!M$ occurring in [def-sf-kv-maps] (iv), whose current statement explicitly specifies these four inputs and identifies their product morphism with $p_X$. The map is formed with the same geometric exceptional adjunction counits as in (ii).

source.place: Proof, first sentence: exceptional Kunneth for $\operatorname{id}_X\times a_Y$

proof.text: Let $H=\RHom_A(Lp_Y^*N,-)$. The morphism $H(a)$ is invertible with inverse $H(a^{-1})$: functoriality sends $a^{-1}a$ and $aa^{-1}$ to identities. By [def-sf-kv-maps] (iv), the canonical map in the statement is exactly $\kappa_{M,N}=H(a)\circ b$. Its inverse is $b^{-1}\circ H(a^{-1})$; composing in either order cancels the adjacent inverse pairs. Hence the specified $\kappa_{M,N}$ is an isomorphism.

source.place: Proof, second sentence: identify the composite with kappa and compose the inverses

proof_origin.place: Proof, both sentences; expanded input checks and inverse calculation
